causes.fix_hint: Check how Line.amount is computed in cart.py and ensure it uses a numeric price.

causes.title: format_money trusts its input without type validation
causes.explanation: format_money assumes a numeric amount and fails with a format-spec error on the first non-numeric value. This is the crash site, not the origin of the bad string.

causes.title: format_money called with non-numeric amount

error_line: IndexError: list index out of range

causes.title: Rank index can equal list length for small groups
causes.explanation: _rank_index uses round(p/100*n) with no upper clamp, so for a route with only one or two samples, p90 or p99 yields index n, which is out of range. The bad index is created here, even though the crash surfaces later in percentile().
causes.fix_hint: Clamp the index to n-1 or switch to a nearest-rank formula such as max(0, ceil(p/100*n)-1).

causes.title: percentile() indexes without bounds protection
causes.explanation: percentile() only guards the empty-list case and then indexes ordered directly with the result of _rank_index. Any out-of-range rank from small inputs therefore raises IndexError at this line.
causes.fix_hint: Clamp the computed rank into the range 0 to len(ordered)-1 before indexing.

causes.title: per_route receives single-sample route groups
causes.explanation: per_route groups filtered API records by route, so a route with one record reaches percentile() with n=1. This input shape is what triggers the out-of-range rank in the percentile calculation.
causes.fix_hint: Handle single-element groups explicitly or ensure the percentile helper is safe for any group size.

causes.title: Empty times list passed to percentile for a route
causes.explanation: per_route builds times from records in each group, but percentile's early return only guards empty lists, and _rank_index(n, 99) with n=1 or small n can yield index equal to n when p/100*n rounds up past the end. For p=100-ish rounding the index can reach len(ordered), so an out-of-range index is produced from the percentile math itself rather than from empty data.
causes.fix_hint: Clamp the rank index to len(ordered)-1 inside _rank_index or percentile.

causes.title: Rank index formula can exceed list bounds
causes.explanation: _rank_index uses int(round(p / 100 * n)) with no clamping, so for p=99 and small n the rounded value can equal n, which is out of range for ordered[...]. The crash at line 31 is the first place this bad index is used.
causes.fix_hint: Use a clamped nearest-rank formula such as min(n - 1, max(0, round(p / 100 * n) - 1)).

causes.title: Unfiltered api list passed to per_route
causes.explanation: build_report feeds per_route the result of filters.clean(filters.only_api(records)), so routes can end up with very few or unusual timing values. Upstream filtering that produces a sparse group makes the percentile computation more fragile.
causes.fix_hint: Guard per_route or percentile so that groups with no valid timings return 0.0 instead of indexing.

causes.title: Parser admits lines with zero response time
causes.explanation: parse_line accepts any digit sequence for ms, so zero or absent timing values can flow into latency lists; this is where a degenerate input is created, though the crash occurs later in percentile.
causes.fix_hint: Validate that ms is present and positive in the parsed record before it reaches stats.
